Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Topeka KS
1036 PM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

-The coolest weather arrives tonight through Saturday with lows 
 falling into the 20s tonight and again Friday night.

-Rain stays south this weekend, keeping dry weather in place until 
 at least the middle of next week.

-Increasing south winds also bring warmer weather back by midweek.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 225 PM CST Thu Nov 12 2026

An amplified meridional mid-level pattern is in place across the 
CONUS today with a trough over the eastern half of the country, 
ridging over the Mountainous West and another deep trough axis 
approaching the west coast. For us, northwest flow continues aloft 
for now. At the surface, a large surface ridge centered over central 
Canada is building into area. The coolest air within this chilly 
pattern will be felt tonight through Saturday. Radiational cooling 
due to clear skies and nearly calm winds tonight should allow 
temperatures to fall into the upper 20s by sunrise Friday. 
Temperatures will then struggle to reach 50 degrees tomorrow 
afternoon before tanking into the mid 20s tomorrow night. These next
two nights will be the first hard freeze for a majority of the area,
which is anomalously late compared to average.

The surface pattern won't change much on Saturday with the ridge 
holding strong just northeast of the area. Aloft, however, the 
western trough will evolve into a closed low over the TX panhandle 
by early Sunday with a surface low also forming well south of the 
area. Lift associated with that system within an area of better 
moisture availability will lead to rain development in TX/OK and 
possibly far southern KS. Confidence remains high that northeast KS 
will stay dry on the north side of that system. Temperatures 
moderate slightly through the weekend, but will possibly be held 
back slightly due to cloud cover in central KS.

Early next week, the center of the large surface ridge will move 
eastward over the far eastern US, but it will still have some grip 
on the area. The approach of another western trough will induce 
cyclogenesis to our west, increasing the pressure gradient. Stronger
southwest flow should boost temperatures back to near 60 degrees by 
the middle of the week. That is also when rain chances start to 
creep back into the forecast, although probabilities remain around 20
to 30 percent with low confidence at this range.
